name: King of Aram
overview: The King of Aram was a male ruler known primarily for his military victory over King Ahaz of Judah, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 28:5. Beyond this notable defeat, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or tribal affiliations. His role is significant in the context of the conflicts involving Judah during this period.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Aram' literally means 'king of Aram,' indicating his position as the sovereign ruler of the Aramean people. This title is descriptive and does not carry a personal name or divine attribution, simply identifying his royal status over Aram as noted in 2 Chronicles 28:5.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Aram beyond what is indicated by his title and unique attribute. There are no specific mentions of relatives or lineage connected to him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Aram's significance lies in his military engagement with Judah, where he successfully defeated King Ahaz. This event highlights the geopolitical tensions faced by Judah and underscores the challenges to its stability during that era. His defeat of Ahaz serves as a historical marker of Aram's strength and influence in the biblical narrative.
